Both disclosures describe AMD's current-generation discrete desktop and notebook GPUs based on the RDNA 3 architecture (Radeon RX 7000 series). The 2023 disclosure details the architecture's features (AI/ray tracing hardware, Infinity Cache) and VRAM targets, while the 2024 disclosure confirms the continued focus on this architecture for gaming and AI/ML computing, supported by the Adrenalin software.

previous_disclosures.summary: AMD Radeon series GPUs support DirectX 12 Ultimate, Vulkan, FreeSync technologies, and VR, supported by Radeon Software tools and open-source FidelityFX toolkit for developers.

The RDNA3 architecture, powering the Radeon RX 7000 series, provides up to 96 compute units, AI/ray tracing hardware, Infinity Cache, and supports AI-accelerated video encoding and AV1 hardware encoding, targeting discrete desktop GPUs with up to 24GB VRAM and notebooks with up to 16GB.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm disclose the inclusion of GPUs within their heterogeneous computing architectures. AMD describes its discrete Radeon GPUs for desktops and notebooks, while Qualcomm describes its integrated Adreno GPUs as part of its Snapdragon System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture designed for high-performance computing and 3D gaming in mobile and other devices.
